name: Automation playbook
goal: The complete how-to for automating one real piece of work with AI, so the reader gets hours back every week. The most bookmarked kind of article: readers save it to set it up later.
angle: Pick ONE task people still do by hand and could hand to AI (posting on X, writing threads, research, replies, reports, video edits, publishing on Instagram) and show the full setup from zero to running on its own: the tools (Claude Code, skills, scripts, schedulers), the exact steps, files, commands and prompts, what it costs, what breaks and how to keep quality up. The owner's own systems are the proof it works: use their real numbers from the data. Verify every command against current official docs.
titles: How to automate X posting to reach maximum productivity
I automated my whole posting week with Claude Code. Here is the exact setup.
Stop posting by hand: the AI setup that runs my account while I sleep
structure: Open with the payoff (what runs by itself at the end and what it saves). Then: why doing it by hand caps you; the setup in numbered steps with the exact tools, files, commands and prompts; the owner's real numbers as proof; what breaks and the fixes; what it costs; a checklist recap.

name: Free alternative
goal: One AI skill or open-source tool that does what people pay a subscription for. People share money-savers and bookmark the setup.
angle: Find ONE real Claude skill, Claude Code plugin, MCP server or open-source AI tool (from the data or your own research) that replaces a paid product: clipping long videos into shorts, captions, thumbnails, editing, transcription, scheduling, research, design. Name the paid product it replaces and what that costs (verified on its pricing page), then show exactly how to install and use the free one, what it does as well, what it does worse, and who should still pay. Only tools you verified exist and work as described: check the repository, its docs and its license.
titles: This Claude skill can clip GTA6 without paying for a product
This free Claude Code skill replaces a $29/month video tool
Stop paying for AI captions: this open-source tool does it locally
structure: Open with the swap in one line (what you stop paying for, what you use instead). Then: what the paid tool does and costs; the free one and why it works; install and first run in numbered steps with the exact commands; a real example from start to finish; where it falls short; who should switch and who should not; recap.

name: Viral breakdown
goal: Reverse engineer a real piece of content that went massively viral and show how to make that kind of content with AI tools. Readers share it because it turns someone else's result into a recipe.
angle: Find ONE real format or account that got huge numbers recently on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts or X (animations, AI videos, edits, carousels, explainers) and verify the numbers from the post itself or reputable reporting. Break down why it spread (hook, format, pacing, emotion, loop) and then how to make it yourself with AI tools (Claude, Claude Code, Remotion, image and video models), step by step, with the exact prompts and settings. The results are the creator's, never the owner's.
titles: How to make animations for Instagram to get 55M views
This AI video format got 120M views. Here is how to make it in an afternoon.
I reverse engineered the most viral AI reels this month. They all do one thing.
structure: Open with the result and who got it (verified number, named account or format). Then: what the content is; why it spread, point by point; how to make it with AI in numbered steps, with prompts and settings; the mistakes that make copies flop; recap as a checklist.

name: Growth myth
goal: A strong, defensible take on growing an audience with AI that goes against what most people believe. Shares and replies come from disagreement backed by evidence.
angle: Take ONE belief most creators hold about growth on Instagram, X, TikTok or YouTube (you need a big following to go viral, posting more is the answer, AI content gets buried, the algorithm hates links...) and show why it is wrong with evidence: what the platforms themselves have said, real accounts and their verified results, and how AI makes the better approach cheap to run. Be fair to the other side, never rage bait, never promise results.
titles: Going viral on Instagram is WAY easier than you think
You don't need followers to go viral. You need this.
Everyone is wrong about AI content and the algorithm
structure: Open with the common belief and why it is wrong, in 2 lines. Then: what the platform actually rewards (verified); real examples with their numbers; the method in numbered steps, with how AI does the heavy lifting; what still does not work; recap.
